items.text: Burned to Ashes

items.speaker: Partita
items.text: You and Franz had a fight?

items.speaker: Charon
items.text: He was wounded. I brought him back.
He avoids answering the question.
Partita opens her mouth, but her face quickly darkens. Charon turns his head.

items.speaker: Lieutenant Colonel Wolker
items.text: These past few days been treating you well? You'll be busy tomorrow when the hospital clears out.

items.speaker: Charon
items.text: Guten Tag, Herr Oberstleutnant. May it pass without incident.
Even Charon, often criticized for his slowness, senses something unusual.

items.speaker: Charon
items.text: You are unarmed?

items.speaker: Lieutenant Colonel Wolker
items.text: Not every day you see an unarmed officer in the trenches, eh?
He smiles.

items.speaker: Lieutenant Colonel Wolker
items.text: The war will be over soon. I'm just waiting for retirement ... my granddaughter's due any day now.

items.speaker: Lieutenant Colonel Wolker
items.text: I'd rather not carry a gun again. Maybe I'll never need to.

items.speaker: Charon
items.text: Your wife's letter ... I remember a pub. Laughter and beer to replace bullets and blood.

items.speaker: Lieutenant Colonel Wolker
items.text: Yes, she knows me well. Once I give up this uniform, all I want is to run a simple pub.

items.speaker: Lieutenant Colonel Wolker
items.text: Chatting with regulars, cracking jokes, a few hands of Skat ...

items.speaker: Lieutenant Colonel Wolker
items.text: I'll waive a tab here and there—give them a reason to bring all their friends and family around.

items.speaker: Charon
items.text: Franz would certainly come.

items.speaker: Lieutenant Colonel Wolker
items.text: Tell him to come, then. I'll serve him up a bratwurst, free of charge.

items.speaker: Lieutenant Colonel Wolker
items.text: We've been at war too long. It's time to remember how we used to live.
Charon glances at Partita. She stands quietly nearby.
Partita knows what he wants to say, but she can't stop herself.

items.speaker: Partita
items.text: Lieutenant Colonel Wolker, you ordered that shelling, didn't you? Even though the intelligence was wrong. You killed your own men.

items.speaker: Partita
items.text: You killed my fiancé, Walter.
Wolker turns slightly to face her.

items.speaker: Lieutenant Colonel Wolker
items.text: A girl who could've attended school alongside my daughter, and yet she looks at me like I'm the enemy.

items.speaker: Lieutenant Colonel Wolker
items.text: Well, I suppose I deserve it. Though, I've rarely had such an encounter.

items.speaker: Partita
items.text: There are surely thousands of girls like me throughout the fatherland. You just haven't met them yet.

items.speaker: Lieutenant Colonel Wolker
items.text: Yes, yes, you're right. I've prepared myself for that.

items.speaker: Partita
items.text: You'd better have.
The lieutenant colonel's gaze follows every trace of coldness and hatred on her face. He smiles bitterly.

items.speaker: Lieutenant Colonel Wolker
items.text: Walter was young, but he had a good head on his shoulders—a sharp and thoughtful lad.

items.speaker: Lieutenant Colonel Wolker
items.text: When he first arrived, he wouldn't even fire his weapon. Ah, but he certainly was no coward.

items.speaker: Partita
items.text: Don't you dare try to play on my emotions.

items.speaker: Lieutenant Colonel Wolker
items.text: We're just the treads on a tank, Partita. We're ordered to advance, and we crush everything in our path.

items.speaker: Lieutenant Colonel Wolker
items.text: On the front, it's win or die, and when someone dies out here, it's never just one person who pays the price.

items.speaker: Lieutenant Colonel Wolker
items.text: I regret Walter's death—more than the men who ordered the advance.

items.speaker: Partita
items.text: So you're shifting the blame now? Telling me it's some other bastard's fault?

items.speaker: Lieutenant Colonel Wolker
items.text: Of course not. War is a river of hatred and death. I stepped into it. I must accept the price.

items.speaker: Lieutenant Colonel Wolker
items.text: If you want to kill me, so be it—but you'll have to step into that river too.

items.speaker: Lieutenant Colonel Wolker
items.text: So, Partita, if you're ready for everything that comes with that, then pull the trigger. I won't stop you.
Partita's lips tremble. She tries to speak, but the words fail to come.
The lieutenant colonel turns and barks the name of a nearby sergeant.

items.speaker: Lieutenant Colonel Wolker
items.text: The firearm you asked for has arrived, Partita. I've come to deliver it to you myself.
She takes the pistol and lightly tests its weight in her hand.
Charon watches as the lieutenant colonel leaves, then turns to Partita.

items.speaker: Charon
items.text: He's just an old man awaiting his retirement.

items.speaker: Partita
items.text: Oh, so you're going to preach to me too?

items.speaker: Charon
items.text: Taking his life will only cause you to suffer.

items.speaker: Partita
items.text: That's it, Paul. Get it all out. After all, how often do you get the chance to sound so noble?

items.speaker: Charon
items.text: Remember our deal? When the field hospital leaves, you leave the battlefield.
She keeps her eyes on the pistol, perhaps studying its parts, or perhaps lost elsewhere.

items.speaker: Partita
items.text: With everything that's happened ... is there even anywhere for me to go back to?

items.speaker: Partita
items.text: I hunted for the truth behind Walter's death because I needed a reason to live.

items.speaker: Partita
items.text: Even if that reason was absurd ... or based purely on hatred.

items.speaker: Partita
items.text: But Wolker still gets to go home.

items.speaker: Charon
items.text: Partita, you can go anywhere you wish—anywhere but this battlefield.

items.speaker: Partita
items.text: I have nowhere to go. Nothing else to live for.

items.speaker: Charon
items.text: Why people choose to live is something beyond my grasp, but the soldiers who walk beside me choose it every day.

items.speaker: Charon
items.text: Some wait to embrace their family again; others dream of tending gardens after the war.

items.speaker: Charon
items.text: For some, even drowning themselves in schnapps from dusk till dawn is a reason to carry on living.

items.speaker: Charon
items.text: The living set goals, and death laughs.

items.speaker: Charon
items.text: But you must have one, all the same. You simply need to find it.

items.speaker: Partita
items.text: Not everyone can bear this kind of pain—or the torment of the endless questions without answers.

items.speaker: Partita
items.text: Paul, you know better than anyone that none of this means a thing.

items.speaker: Partita
items.text: You already admitted as much. You're only saying this because you pity me.

items.speaker: Partita
items.text: Maybe my reason for living is ridiculous, but is enduring suffering purely for the sake of living any better?
With a flick of her wrist, the magazine ejects. She empties it, leaving only one bullet.
She puts the rest into Charon's pocket, then lifts her gaze to meet his.
Her eyes are calm.

items.speaker: Partita
items.text: Time for me to go.

items.speaker: Wilhelm
items.text: Why's everyone looking so grim?
The soldier cuts into the conversation.

items.speaker: Charon
items.text: The hospital is moving out. The time has come for us to part ways.

items.speaker: Wilhelm
items.text: Did you give that photo to Fabien?

items.speaker: Charon
items.text: He will see it soon.

items.speaker: Wilhelm
items.text: Good. Give my best to him, won't you? ... Have you seen Wolker about?

items.speaker: Charon
items.text: He is down in the bunker.
Partita takes a few steps backward as she tries to slip away unnoticed.

items.speaker: Wilhelm
items.text: Ah, well, his gun's fixed—good as new. I brought it back for him.

items.speaker: Wilhelm
items.text: Seems the lieutenant colonel only trusts his own pistol. He refused to accept any of the spares.
His words hang heavy in the air.

items.speaker: Charon
items.text: What do you mean?

items.speaker: Partita
items.text: I thought he said he was done with all this! He said he wasn't carrying a weapon because the war was ending and he was going home!

items.speaker: Wilhelm
items.text: Eh? What are you two talking about?
He looks like he's just heard a joke he doesn't understand.

items.speaker: Wilhelm
items.text: He's not retiring; he's just moving to the rear. Why would he quit now?

items.speaker: Wilhelm
items.text: They're putting him up for a medal—he'll be a full colonel by fall.
The fog in Charon's mind thickens.

items.speaker: Charon
items.text: You guess at what you don't know, don't you, Willi?

items.speaker: Wilhelm
items.text: Charon, I'm the man's orderly, for heaven's sake. I know him.
Perhaps, at this moment, Charon shouldn't be questioning Wilhelm. Perhaps he should be watching Partita.

items.speaker: Partita
items.text: That damned liar! That sneaky, two-faced swine!
But would stopping her really change anything?

items.speaker: Charon
items.text: Partita—
She slips into the bunker as swift as a breeze.
Words enter Charon's mind in a stampede. The world starts to spin.
"Walter is dead."

"'Friendly fire,' they said. But nothing about it was friendly—not when they dropped it while we advanced!"

"Verdammt! Why didn't I pull him into the crater when I had the chance? Verdammt nochmal! Verdammt!"

"I could've had him—just one more second and he'd still be here!"

"Gott im Himmel ... what do I tell Partita? How do I tell his mother?"

"I lived ... and Walter died?"

"Or should I tell them I'm sorry—that he should've been the one who lived?"

"It's true ... it shouldn't have been him. He was the one who kept us going, kept us smiling."
In the echo of the shot, it all falls silent. The noise, the whispers, the thoughts—everything.
Charon sees the lieutenant colonel clutching his chest, red pouring out from between his fingers.
Partita turns to Charon, her face now calm and distant.
Both the living and the dead fall silent.
